names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 13 mai, «Sfânta Muceniță Glicheria».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Μαΐου, «Αγία Γλυκερία», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 13 May, „Света мученица Гликерија.“ — Света left off, which is not a rank, and мученица left off, which is the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types`. The heading gives no epithet and no city: Rome, Traianopolis, Thrace, Antoninus and the 177 are all in the body. A direct walk of every `names` entry in `saints/` finds no folder holding Гликерија, so the form folds with nothing — neither `glyceria-of-adrianople` nor `glyceria-of-novgorod` nor `glycerius-the-farmer`, the three the name sweep raised, has a Serbian form.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name link 2445 as the day page prints it, «Мученица Гликерия Гераклейская», with the rank word left off. The day's own line declines her «Мц. Гликерии девы и с нею мч. Лаодикия , стража темничного (ок. 177).», giving the name with «девы» and no epithet; the epithet is the name page's. Her two life pages are headed «Мученица Гликерия, дева» and «Мученица Гликерия Гераклейская». `fk.mjs` on «Гликерия Гераклейская» returned NONE before the write.

death.note: The first date this folder has carried. The Ohrid Prologue, for the Julian 13 May: „Чесно пострада 177. године.“ Neither doxologia.ro's line for 13 mai nor saint.gr's gave any year at all. The entry also sets her „У време нечестивог цара Антонина“, in the time of the impious emperor Antoninus, and gives that reign no bounds, so nothing was built on it; the 177 is the only number on the page. No birth is recorded and none is printed.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 мая ст. ст. — «Мц. Гликерии девы и с нею мч. Лаодикия , стража темничного (ок. 177).»

attestations.note: The same menologion day the folder already keeps for the other three churches, and the same woman: the virgin who broke the idol of Zeus by her prayer, was kept alive in prison by angels, and was killed by the second lioness in the arena at Heraclea. The Russian name page heads her «Мученица Гликерия Гераклейская», of Heraclea where she died, against this folder's Traianopolis where she lived; both are in the life. **The source contradicts itself on the date and `dates` were not touched.** Its fuller life page, life1055, opens «пострадала за Христову веру во II веке во время гонения на христиан императора Антонина (138 - 161)» and closes «Она пострадала за Христа около 177 года» — a persecution under Antoninus, who was dead sixteen years before the year the same page ends with. The day line gives «(ок. 177)». The folder already carries 177 off the Ohrid Prologue, whose own note records the same internal disagreement in the Serbian book, so nothing is widened and both readings now stand in the life. **Two hymns were copied**, the troparion and the kontakion the day page prints «мученицы Гликерии девы»; the troparion is the common of a virgin martyr with her name set into it, which BRIEF.md §4 takes as hers. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 13 mai — «Sfânta Muceniță Glicheria»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Μαΐου — «Αγία Γλυκερία»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps her on, and its synaxarion verse agrees: «Ἐν τριτάτῃ δεκάτῃ δάκε καὶ κτάνε θὴρ Γλυκερίαν». It is plainly the same woman, the virgin martyr of Traianopolis thrown to the beasts. **She is not the day's other Glyceria**: saint.gr keeps on this same 13 May a Glyceria of Novgorod, daughter of a municipal officer, dead in peace in 1522, who is a new folder in batch `el-05-13`; and the corpus's Glyceria of Adrianople is a third woman on 22 October. **The Greek adds the years the corpus does not hold**: «(; - 141)» in its head line, a birth at Traianopolis in the second century under Antoninus Pius (138–161), and a consul father named Makarios. The existing folder carries no `dates` object and it is not given one here; the years stand in this note and in the added paragraph. **It names her jailer**, Laodicius, whom the same day keeps and who is a new folder in the same batch; he is linked. **It names the bishop who took up her relic**, Domitios of Heraclea, who has no folder and is named without a link. **Two apolytikia stand on the page and only one is taken**: the first, Ἦχος γ’ Τὴν ὡραιότητα, names her — «χαίροις θεόφρον Γλυκερία» — and is copied; the Έτερον in Ἦχος δ’ is «Ἡ ἀμνάς σου Ἰησοῦ», the common of a woman martyr, and is left, the folder needing no second hymn to say the same thing. Neither is a mis-hang. The page also gives her as patron of Galatsi in Attica.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.05.2026 (13. мај ст. ст.) — „Света мученица Гликерија.“

attestations.note: The day's first entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek both keep her on, so nothing moved. **A FIRST DATE FOR A FOLDER THAT HELD NONE**: „Чесно пострада 177. године“ → `death` 177, where this folder had no `dates` object at all and neither the Romanian nor the Greek line gave a year. It sits inside the reign the entry itself names — „У време нечестивог цара Антонина“ — and nothing was reckoned from that reign, which the book gives with no bounds. **New here, and the whole of the account**: that she was the daughter of a governor of Rome and settled at Traianopolis in Thrace when her father died and left her an orphan; that she drew a cross on her own forehead, and when the emperor's deputy asked where her lamp was — for all of them carried lamps in their hands — showed him the cross and said „Ово је моја лампада“, this is my lamp; that at her prayer thunder struck the idol of Zeus and broke it in pieces; that she was beaten and thrown into prison, and the deputy **sealed the prison doors** meaning to kill her by hunger, and an angel of God came to her and gave her heavenly food, so that when he opened the prison he was astonished to find her healthy, bright and cheerful; that she was cast into a fiery furnace and stood unhurt in the middle of it praising God and **recalling the three youths in the Babylonian furnace**; that she was at last thrown before lions and gave up her soul after praying; and that **healing myrrh flowed from her relics**, which cured the sick of the gravest diseases. **`related_add` is not used and nothing was invented**: `laodicius-the-jailer` was already a `related` row on this folder in both directions, and the three youths are named as a company and not individually, so no row is owed for them. `types` untouched: Света is no rank, мученица is the `martyr` the folder carries, and `virgin` is corroborated by „ова света дева“. **No `locations`**: Rome and Traianopolis are named and this folder has never claimed a point. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Glicheria, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc, și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

english.text: Thy lamb, O Jesus, Glyceria, cries out with a loud voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, I love, and seeking Thee I am in torment; I am crucified with Thee and buried with Thee in Thy baptism; I suffer for Thee that I may reign in Thee, and I die for Thee that I may live for Thee. Receive me as a spotless sacrifice, who offer myself to Thee in love. At her prayers, O merciful one, save our souls.

hymns.text: Τὴν καλλιπάρθενον, Χριστοῦ τιμήσωμεν, τὴν ἀριστεύσασαν πόνοις ἀθλήσεως, καὶ ἀσθενείᾳ τῆς σαρκός, τὸν ὄφιν καταβαλοῦσαν· πόθω γὰρ τοῦ Κτίσαντος, τῶν βασάνων τὴν ἔφοδον, παρ’ οὐδὲν ἡγήσατο, καὶ θεόθεν δεδόξασται· πρὸς ἣν ἀναβοήσωμεν πάντες, χαίροις θεόφρον Γλυκερία.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Τὴν ὡραιότητα, on the page of Αγία Γλυκερία

english.text: Let us honour Christ's fair virgin, who excelled in the labours of her contest and, in the weakness of the flesh, threw down the serpent; for out of longing for her Maker she counted the onset of the torments as nothing, and has been glorified by God. To her let us all cry aloud: rejoice, God-minded Glyceria.

hymns.text: Агница Твоя, Иисусе, Гликерия,/ зовет велиим гласом:/ Тебе, Женише мой, люблю,/ и, Тебе ищущи, страдальчествую,/ и сраспинаюся, и спогребаюся крещению Твоему,/ и стражду Тебе ради,/ яко да царствую в Тебе, и умираю за Тя,/ да и живу с Тобою,/ но, яко жертву непорочную, приими мя, с любовию пожершуюся Тебе./ Тоя молитвами,/ яко Милостив, спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 мая ст. ст. — «Тропарь мученицы Гликерии девы»; it is the common of a virgin martyr with her name set into it

english.text: Thy lamb, O Jesus, Glyceria, cries out with a loud voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, do I love, and seeking Thee I suffer; I am crucified and buried together with Thee in Thy baptism, and I suffer for Thy sake that I may reign in Thee, and I die for Thee that I may also live with Thee. Receive me as an unblemished sacrifice, offered to Thee in love. By her prayers, as Thou art merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Деву любящи и Богородицу Марию,/ соблюла еси нетленно твое девство,/ любовию же ко Господу усердствовавши,/ пострадала еси мужемудренно даже до смерти./ Сего ради и сугубым тя, дево мученице, венцем венчает Христос Бог.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 мая ст. ст. — «Кондак мученицы Гликерии девы»

english.text: Loving the Virgin and Mother of God Mary, thou didst keep thy virginity undefiled; and being zealous in thy love toward the Lord, thou didst suffer with a manly wisdom even unto death. For this Christ God crowns thee, O virgin martyr, with a double crown.
